graph.title: LEGO City 60054-1 Light Repair Truck

parts.label: Lamp post base tile with bar

notes: The two groups are intentional. The booklet builds two separate models: the Light Repair Truck (steps 1-26) and the street light with traffic light (page 29 onward, with its own step numbering 1-5). The last page shows the street light standing on its own plate, not attached to the truck. Joining them would add a connection the manual does not show, so I kept them as two groups.

The wrench (lego-4006, b79) is held by the minifigure, which is not in the supplied parts list and has no node. To keep it from floating, I added a `contact` edge to the steering stand (b17), since the minifigure sits in the cab. This is an assumption.
The sticker sheet (b91) is one node, joined to the bumper (b28), hood (b35) and roof wedge (b42). The manual only shows sticker positions.
Most stud and anti-stud joins use null ports because the exact stud positions can't be read from the pictures. Which piece a part sits on is inferred from the isometric views.
The vehicle base (b1) was given only null ports because its port list is truncated in the catalogue.

I assigned the 3 trans-red plates as one on the centre orange plate (b6) and two on the rear plate (b3). The assignment of b29 and b30 to the left and right white plates and of the doors to the clip plates is a guess from the pictures.

The windscreen (b41) has no catalogue ports. I joined it to the hood plate (b31) and one hinge plate (b32). The roof wedge (b42) is shown lifting off in the last view, so it is attached to b39 and b41 and can be removed.
The boom pivots: the blue pin (b55) goes through both pin-hole plates (b50, b51) and carries the 6536 connector (b60). The pin (b59) joins b60 to the second arm (b61).
The Gmail, Google Calendar and Google Drive connectors need authorization through the claude.ai connector settings. They are unavailable until then and were not needed for this task.
